avoid: Complex interlocking that might cause frustration
children.game_version: Shadow puppets: create shapes and have others guess the object.

seniors.seated_version: Inherently performed seated; excellent for fine motor skill maintenance.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce tempo to 60 BPM; focus on gentle joint mobility rather than sharp snaps.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Arms are often held in fixed 'tut' positions (90-degree angles at elbows and wrists) to provide a frame for the fingers.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Small, localized space directly in front of the dancer's body.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: None; focus is entirely on the upper body and hands.
movement_profile.partnering: Primarily solo, though synchronized group routines exist.
movement_profile.posture: Usually seated or standing with the torso still to frame the hands.

signature_moves.description: Creating a perfect square using the thumbs and index fingers.
signature_moves.name: The King Tut Box

signature_moves.description: A sequential rippling movement through the fingers from pinky to thumb.
signature_moves.name: Digital Waves

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid rounded or soft angles; the style requires 'hard' 90-degree corners to maintain the illusion.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Sharp, percussive hits with occasional glitchy or rapid subdivisions.
music_profile.sound_description: The music is characterized by crisp, clean electronic beats that provide clear 'points' for the dancer to hit. It often features a heavy emphasis on the snare or 'click' sounds to mirror the snapping movements of the finger joints.
music_profile.vocal_style: Often instrumental or with rhythmic vocal samples.

basic_steps: The Box: Create a square shape using the index fingers and thumbs of both hands.
The Staircase: Stack fingers horizontally one above the other in a stepped pattern.
The Pivot: Rotate one hand 90 degrees while keeping a finger joint connected to the other hand.
Finger Isolation: Lift or fold one finger at a time while keeping the others perfectly still.
teaching.formation: Solo, usually facing a camera or audience at chest height.
teaching.level_notes: Beginners should focus on hand flexibility and basic 90-degree boxes before attempting rapid transitions.
teaching.rhythm: Syncopated, hitting sharp accents in the music.
